subtopic_detail: First line ovulation induction agent in anovulatory polycystic ovary syndrome
stem:
You are the gynaecology registrar seeing a 29 year old woman who has been trying to conceive for 14 months. She has had four or five periods a year since her teens and shaves her chin every second day.

Her body mass index was 34 kg/m2 at her first visit six months ago and is now 31 kg/m2 after a supervised diet and exercise programme, and her cycles remain unchanged. Her partner's semen analysis was normal on two occasions. A hysterosalpingogram showed a normal cavity with free spill from both tubes. She is rubella immune, takes folic acid, and her thyroid function and prolactin are within normal limits.

data_table.Examination: Body mass index 31 kg/m2, terminal hair over the chin and lower abdomen, no acanthosis nigricans, normal sized non tender uterus and adnexae
data_table.Investigations: Thyroid stimulating hormone 1.9 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), prolactin 320 mIU/L (less than 500), total testosterone mildly raised, transvaginal ultrasound showing multifollicular ovaries with normal antral morphology, hysterosalpingogram with bilateral free spill

options.text: Ovulation induction with letrozole and follicle tracking by ultrasound
options.rationale: An aromatase inhibitor is first line for ovulation induction in this condition on the strength of higher live birth rates than the older agent, particularly in women with a raised body mass index, and cycles are monitored to limit multiple follicular development (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: Ovulation induction with clomifene and follicle tracking by ultrasound
options.rationale: The selective oestrogen receptor modulator was first line for decades and remains effective, but head to head trials show lower ovulation and live birth rates than the aromatase inhibitor, partly because its anti oestrogenic effect thins the endometrium and cervical mucus (Source: International Evidence Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome).
source_refs: International Evidence Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

options.text: Metformin alone with a review of her cycles again in six months
options.rationale: Metformin improves menstrual regularity and metabolic parameters and can be added to ovulation induction, but as sole therapy it is inferior for achieving live birth (Source: International Evidence Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome).
source_refs: International Evidence Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

options.text: Referral for in vitro fertilisation as the next treatment step
options.rationale: Assisted reproduction is third line in this setting, reserved for failure of oral agents and gonadotrophins or for a coexisting indication, and it carries a substantial risk of ovarian hyperstimulation in these women (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: Ovulation induction with injectable gonadotrophins and monitoring
options.rationale: Gonadotrophins are second line after failure of an oral agent, and using them first exposes her to a higher multiple pregnancy and hyperstimulation risk with intensive monitoring that oral treatment avoids (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

explanation.summary: Polycystic ovary syndrome is the commonest cause of anovulatory infertility and is diagnosed on two of three criteria: oligo or anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound, after excluding thyroid disease, hyperprolactinaemia and non classical congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Lifestyle intervention comes first because a loss of five to ten per cent of body weight restores ovulation in a substantial proportion, and it improves the response to every subsequent treatment. Where lifestyle alone does not restore ovulation, pharmacological induction proceeds in a defined order, and treatment is only started once tubal patency and semen analysis are known so that a couple is not put through cycles that cannot succeed. Cycle monitoring is required because these ovaries are exquisitely sensitive and multiple pregnancy is the main avoidable complication.
key_points: Diagnosis requires two of three criteria after exclusion of thyroid, prolactin and adrenal causes.
Weight loss of five to ten per cent restores ovulation in a meaningful proportion of women.
An aromatase inhibitor is first line for ovulation induction, ahead of the older oral agent.
Semen analysis and tubal patency are established before induction begins.
Follicle tracking limits multiple pregnancy in ovaries that are highly sensitive to stimulation.
explanation.pearls: Letrozole is given on cycle days two to six and works by transiently lowering oestrogen to release the pituitary from negative feedback, and because its half life is around 45 hours it has cleared well before implantation, which is why the early teratogenicity concern was not borne out.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
International Evidence Based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome

subtopic_detail: Sequencing antibiotics before surgical evacuation in secondary postpartum haemorrhage
stem:
You are the obstetric registrar called to the emergency department to see a 26 year old woman who gave birth 12 days ago. She had a spontaneous vaginal birth at term and the placenta appeared complete at the time.

Her lochia had almost stopped by day eight but for the past two days she has been soaking a maternity pad every hour with bright red blood and passing clots the size of a golf ball. Her partner says the discharge smells offensive. She has had rigors overnight. Her uterus is tender and the fundus is palpable midway between the symphysis and the umbilicus. A transvaginal ultrasound shows heterogeneous echogenic material 22 mm across within the cavity with vascularity on colour Doppler.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse rate 106 beats per minute, blood pressure 108/64 mmHg, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, SpO2 98 per cent on room air, temperature 38.2 degrees Celsius
data_table.Examination: Tender bulky uterus with the fundus midway to the umbilicus, open cervical os with active bright red loss, offensive discharge, no adnexal masses
data_table.Investigations: Haemoglobin 92 g/L (115-165), white cell count 16.8 x10^9/L (4.0-11.0), C reactive protein 122 mg/L (less than 5), high vaginal and endocervical swabs and blood cultures collected

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Observation with repeat full blood count and ultrasound in a week
options.rationale: Expectant management is reasonable for retained tissue found incidentally in a well woman with light loss, and this presentation with sepsis and heavy ongoing bleeding is the near pair that it must be distinguished from (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: Intravenous antibiotics with evacuation by a senior obstetrician
options.rationale: Retained products with endometritis need broad spectrum intravenous cover started immediately, and because the bleeding is heavy and continuing, evacuation follows rather than waiting, performed by an experienced operator because the infected postpartum uterus perforates easily (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: Immediate evacuation of the uterus before antibiotics are given
options.rationale: Instrumenting an infected uterus without antibiotic cover risks bacteraemia and septic shock, so the first dose goes in before the patient goes to theatre (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).
source_refs: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic

options.text: Oral antibiotics with discharge and community midwife review
options.rationale: Oral therapy at home is appropriate for mild endometritis in a woman who is afebrile and not bleeding heavily, and she is tachycardic, febrile, rigoring and anaemic (Source: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic).
source_refs: Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic

options.text: Intramuscular ergometrine with repeat ultrasound in seven days
options.rationale: A uterotonic may reduce loss transiently but does not clear retained tissue or treat the infection driving it, and a week of delay in a woman already at 92 g/L is unsafe (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

explanation.summary: Secondary postpartum haemorrhage is bleeding from 24 hours to 12 weeks after birth, and the two dominant causes, retained products and endometritis, usually coexist because retained tissue provides the substrate for infection. Ultrasound has limited specificity in the puerperium since clot and normal involuting decidua can look identical to retained tissue, so vascularity on colour Doppler is the finding that most raises the likelihood of true retained products. The decision to operate balances the risk of continued bleeding against the risk of perforation and later intrauterine adhesions, both of which are considerably higher in a soft infected postpartum uterus. Where the bleeding is settling and the woman is stable, antibiotics alone allow many cases to resolve without instrumentation.
key_points: Secondary postpartum haemorrhage spans 24 hours to 12 weeks after birth.
Retained products and endometritis usually coexist and are treated together.
Colour Doppler vascularity raises the likelihood that echogenic material is retained tissue rather than clot.
Antibiotics are started before instrumentation to avoid precipitating bacteraemia.
Evacuation of an infected soft uterus is performed by an experienced operator because of perforation risk.
explanation.pearls: Intrauterine adhesions follow puerperal curettage in up to a fifth of cases, far more than after a non pregnant procedure, which is why gentle suction with the largest safe cannula under ultrasound guidance is preferred to sharp curettage.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

subtopic_detail: Choosing emergency contraception at four days with a raised body mass index
stem:
You are the general practice registrar seeing a 24 year old woman who had unprotected intercourse four days ago, on day 12 of a regular 28 day cycle.

She has been using condoms alone and one broke. Her body mass index is 36 kg/m2. She has no history of pelvic inflammatory disease and no unusual discharge, and a self collected swab for chlamydia and gonorrhoea has been sent today with results due tomorrow. A urine pregnancy test today is negative. She tells you she would like something more reliable going forward and is open to any method.

data_table.Examination: Body mass index 36 kg/m2, normal sized anteverted uterus, no adnexal tenderness, no cervical motion tenderness, no abnormal discharge
data_table.Investigations: Urine beta human chorionic gonadotrophin negative, chlamydia and gonorrhoea nucleic acid testing pending

options.text: Levonorgestrel 3 mg orally as a single dose taken today
options.rationale: Doubling the dose is sometimes used at higher body weight, but the supporting evidence is weak and the underlying limitation, that it only works if given before the luteinising hormone surge, still applies on day 12 (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).
source_refs: Australian Medicines Handbook

options.text: Reassurance that emergency contraception is no longer effective
options.rationale: Four days is still inside the window for a copper device, so declaring the opportunity closed would deny her the most effective option available (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: A copper intrauterine device inserted within the next 24 hours
options.rationale: The copper device can be inserted up to five days after intercourse or up to five days after the earliest calculated ovulation, has a failure rate below one per cent that is unaffected by body weight, and simultaneously provides the ongoing contraception she has asked for (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: Ulipristal acetate 30 mg orally as a single dose taken today
options.rationale: This agent is licensed to 120 hours and is the better of the two oral options, but its efficacy falls as body mass index rises above 30 kg/m2 and it remains substantially less effective than the device (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).
source_refs: Australian Medicines Handbook

options.text: Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg orally as a single dose taken today
options.rationale: Oral levonorgestrel is licensed only to 96 hours and its efficacy declines markedly above a body mass index of 26 kg/m2, so both timing and body weight work against it here (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).
source_refs: Australian Medicines Handbook

explanation.summary: Emergency contraception has three options in Australia and they differ in mechanism, window and reliability. The two oral agents work by delaying or preventing ovulation, which means both fail if the luteinising hormone surge has already begun, and both lose efficacy as body weight rises. The copper intrauterine device works by a direct toxic effect on gametes and by preventing implantation, so it is unaffected by weight and by where the woman is in her cycle, and it is more than ten times more effective than either oral agent. A pending sexually transmitted infection result does not delay insertion; the device is inserted and treatment is given if the result returns positive. Any woman offered emergency contraception should also leave with a plan for ongoing contraception, since the encounter is often the only opportunity.
key_points: The copper device is effective up to five days after intercourse and is unaffected by body weight.
Oral levonorgestrel is licensed to 96 hours; ulipristal to 120 hours.
Both oral agents lose efficacy at higher body mass index and fail after the luteinising hormone surge.
A pending infection screen does not delay device insertion.
Every emergency contraception consultation includes a plan for ongoing contraception.
explanation.pearls: Ulipristal is a progesterone receptor modulator, so starting a progestogen containing method within five days after it blunts its effect, and hormonal contraception is deferred for that interval with condoms used in the meantime.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

subtopic_detail: Referral for fetoscopic laser at an early stage of twin to twin transfusion syndrome
stem:
You are the obstetric registrar reviewing a 31 year old woman in her first pregnancy at 19 weeks and 2 days with a monochorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy, attending for her routine fortnightly surveillance scan.

She feels well, has no abdominal tightening, no bleeding and no leaking. Her fundal height is larger than expected for dates and she has noticed her abdomen becoming rapidly more distended over the past fortnight. Today's scan reports the first twin with a deepest vertical pocket of 1.4 cm and a bladder that is not visible over 60 minutes of observation, and the second twin with a deepest vertical pocket of 9.2 cm and a persistently distended bladder. Umbilical artery Doppler waveforms show positive end diastolic flow in both twins, the ductus venosus waveforms are normal, and neither twin is hydropic.

data_table.Vital signs: Maternal pulse rate 88 beats per minute, blood pressure 112/68 mmHg, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, SpO2 99 per cent on room air, temperature 36.7 degrees Celsius
data_table.Ultrasound findings: Monochorionic diamniotic twins, twin one deepest vertical pocket 1.4 cm with non visible bladder, twin two deepest vertical pocket 9.2 cm with distended bladder, positive end diastolic flow in both umbilical arteries, normal ductus venosus waveforms, no hydrops, cervical length 34 mm

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Serial amnioreduction with weekly ultrasound surveillance instead
options.rationale: Amnioreduction relieves maternal discomfort and pressure but leaves the shared placental anastomoses intact, and randomised comparison showed laser to give superior survival and less neurological morbidity (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: Weekly ultrasound surveillance with review again in four weeks
options.rationale: Expectant surveillance is reasonable only for isolated discordant growth or for the mildest stage in selected cases, and untreated disease at this stage carries a perinatal mortality above 80 per cent (Source: International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology Practice Guidelines).
source_refs: International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology Practice Guidelines

options.text: Administer antenatal corticosteroids and plan birth at 26 weeks
options.rationale: Birth is not a treatment option at 19 weeks and steroids are given for anticipated preterm birth from 23 weeks, so this plan neither treats the condition nor is deliverable now (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: Amniotic septostomy with weekly ultrasound surveillance instead
options.rationale: Deliberately perforating the dividing membrane equalises fluid volumes but creates a functionally monoamniotic pregnancy with cord entanglement risk and does not treat the vascular cause (Source: International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology Practice Guidelines).
source_refs: International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology Practice Guidelines

options.text: Urgent referral to a foetal therapy centre for laser ablation
options.rationale: A deepest vertical pocket below 2 cm in one sac with above 8 cm in the other before 20 weeks defines the syndrome, and once the donor bladder is no longer visible the disease has advanced beyond the earliest stage, at which point fetoscopic laser ablation of the placental anastomoses gives the best survival (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

explanation.summary: Twin to twin transfusion syndrome complicates around 10 to 15 per cent of monochorionic pregnancies and arises from unbalanced arteriovenous anastomoses within a shared placenta, which is why chorionicity determined in the first trimester dictates the entire surveillance schedule. Diagnosis requires a deepest vertical pocket below 2 cm in one sac with above 8 cm in the other before 20 weeks, using 10 cm as the upper threshold after 20 weeks, and discordant growth alone is not sufficient. Staging runs from isolated fluid discordance, through loss of the donor bladder, abnormal Dopplers, hydrops, to demise of either twin. Fetoscopic laser ablation is the definitive treatment because it addresses the anastomoses themselves, and outcomes are best when it is performed in a high volume centre, which is why monochorionic pregnancies are scanned fortnightly from 16 weeks so that referral happens early.
key_points: Chorionicity is established in the first trimester and drives the surveillance schedule.
Fortnightly ultrasound from 16 weeks is standard in monochorionic pregnancies.
Diagnosis requires deepest vertical pockets below 2 cm and above 8 cm before 20 weeks.
Loss of the donor bladder marks progression beyond the earliest stage.
Fetoscopic laser ablation treats the underlying anastomoses and outperforms amnioreduction.
explanation.pearls: Selective foetal growth restriction is the important near pair and shows discordant estimated weights with normal amniotic fluid volumes, whereas this condition is defined by the fluid discordance and may occur with barely discordant weights.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology Practice Guidelines

subtopic_detail: Antithyroid drug choice by trimester in newly diagnosed hyperthyroidism
stem:
You are the obstetric medicine registrar seeing a 30 year old woman at 7 weeks in her first pregnancy, referred by her general practitioner with palpitations and weight loss.

She has lost 3 kg since her booking visit despite eating normally and describes her heart racing when she climbs the stairs at work. She has a fine tremor of the outstretched hands, warm moist palms and a smooth symmetrically enlarged thyroid with a bruit over it. There is mild retraction of both upper eyelids and slight proptosis. Her vomiting settled at six weeks and she is now keeping food down, and there is no history of a molar pregnancy.

data_table.Vital signs: Pulse rate 112 beats per minute, blood pressure 118/64 mmHg, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, SpO2 99 per cent on room air, temperature 36.9 degrees Celsius
data_table.Investigations: Thyroid stimulating hormone less than 0.01 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), free thyroxine 38 pmol/L (10-20), free triiodothyronine 12.4 pmol/L (3.5-6.5), thyroid stimulating hormone receptor antibody strongly positive
data_table.Examination: Smooth symmetrical goitre with an audible bruit, fine outstretched hand tremor, bilateral lid retraction with mild proptosis

lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Start propylthiouracil now and reassess the plan after 16 weeks
options.rationale: Autoimmune hyperthyroidism in the first trimester is treated with propylthiouracil because the alternative thionamide is associated with aplasia cutis and choanal and oesophageal atresia during organogenesis, with a switch considered after the first trimester to limit hepatotoxicity risk (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

options.text: Start carbimazole now and reassess the plan again after 16 weeks
options.rationale: This is the preferred agent outside pregnancy and after the first trimester, and the two are near pairs whose order is reversed by gestation, since its embryopathy risk is concentrated between 6 and 10 weeks (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).
source_refs: Australian Medicines Handbook

options.text: Start propranolol alone and reassess the plan after 16 weeks
options.rationale: A beta blocker controls tremor and tachycardia and is a useful adjunct for a few weeks, but it does not reduce thyroid hormone production and leaves the pregnancy exposed to the risks of untreated thyrotoxicosis (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).
source_refs: Australian Medicines Handbook

options.text: Arrange radioiodine ablation and reassess the plan after 16 weeks
options.rationale: Radioiodine is absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy because it crosses the placenta and ablates the foetal thyroid, which begins concentrating iodine from around 10 to 12 weeks (Source: Australian Medicines Handbook).
source_refs: Australian Medicines Handbook

options.text: Withhold treatment now and reassess the plan again after 16 weeks
options.rationale: The near pair is transient gestational thyrotoxicosis from human chorionic gonadotrophin, which resolves without treatment, but that condition has no goitre, no eye signs and no receptor antibody, all of which are present here (Source: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists).
source_refs: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists

explanation.summary: Hyperthyroidism in early pregnancy has two dominant causes that need opposite management. Transient gestational thyrotoxicosis reflects cross stimulation of the thyroid stimulating hormone receptor by human chorionic gonadotrophin, peaks around 10 weeks, is associated with hyperemesis and resolves spontaneously without antithyroid drugs. Autoimmune disease persists, has a goitre, sometimes eye signs, and a positive receptor antibody, and it requires treatment because untreated maternal thyrotoxicosis increases miscarriage, pre eclampsia, preterm birth, foetal growth restriction and heart failure. The antithyroid drug is titrated to keep free thyroxine in the upper part of the non pregnant reference range using the smallest possible dose, because both agents cross the placenta and can cause foetal hypothyroidism and goitre if the mother is over treated.
key_points: Propylthiouracil is preferred in the first trimester; carbimazole is preferred thereafter and outside pregnancy.
Radioiodine is absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy and for six months before conception.
Transient gestational thyrotoxicosis has no goitre, no eye signs and no receptor antibody.
The dose is titrated to keep free thyroxine at the upper end of the reference range.
Untreated disease raises risks of miscarriage, pre eclampsia, preterm birth and growth restriction.
explanation.pearls: Thyroid stimulating hormone receptor antibody crosses the placenta and is measured at 18 to 22 weeks and again at 30 to 34 weeks, because a titre more than three times the upper limit predicts foetal and neonatal thyrotoxicosis even in a mother whose own disease is well controlled or previously ablated.

sources.label: Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists
